packages.title: 2025 provisional territorial GHG 367 MtCO2e QA
facts: DESNZ provisionally estimates 2025 UK net territorial greenhouse gas emissions at about 367 MtCO2e.
The estimate is territorial, covering emissions occurring within UK borders.
The 2025 figure is provisional rather than final inventory evidence.
The release uses CO2e for greenhouse-gas totals.
A national territorial total is not a parcel measurement.

packages.title: 2025 provisional GHG 2 percent annual fall QA
facts: DESNZ reports a provisional 2% decrease in net territorial GHG emissions from 2024 to 2025.
The absolute decrease is reported at about 7 MtCO2e.
The comparison is annual and UK territorial in scope.
The provisional series is subject to revision when final estimates are published.
The national trend is not assigned to individual properties.

packages.title: 2025 domestic transport 31 percent share QA
facts: Domestic transport is provisionally reported as 31% of UK net GHG emissions in 2025.
This is a TES sector share rather than a parcel allocation.
The figure is based on provisional 2025 territorial estimates.
Domestic transport is distinct from international aviation and shipping treatment.
No local emissions value is inferred from the national percentage.

packages.title: 2025 buildings and product uses 22 percent QA
facts: Buildings and product uses are provisionally reported as 22% of 2025 UK net GHG emissions.
The TES sector is defined on a by-source basis.
Electricity-use emissions in buildings are generally attributed to electricity supply rather than the building sector.
External temperature affects heating-related building emissions.
The sector share is not an operational parcel measurement.

packages.title: 2025 agriculture 13 percent provisional share QA
facts: Agriculture is provisionally reported as 13% of 2025 UK net GHG emissions.
The provisional methodology uses projections for some non-energy emissions.
Agriculture is a high-level TES sector.
Provisional sector estimates do not follow the full final-inventory methodology.
No farm parcel value is inferred from the national share.

packages.title: 2025 industry 11 percent provisional share QA
facts: Industry is provisionally reported as 11% of 2025 UK net GHG emissions.
The estimate is territorial and by source.
Industry activity and energy use are inputs to emissions estimation but are not themselves CO2e.
Final 2025 estimates are scheduled after full inventory processing.
No industrial parcel value is created from the national share.

packages.title: 2025 electricity supply 10 percent provisional share QA
facts: Electricity supply is provisionally reported as 10% of UK net GHG emissions in 2025.
The sector's emissions are attributed where electricity is generated rather than where electricity is consumed.
The release states electricity-supply emissions fell substantially since 1990.
Generation mix is an important driver of sector emissions.
The national sector estimate is not a parcel-level electricity emissions value.

packages.title: 2025 fuel supply 7 percent provisional share QA
facts: Fuel supply is provisionally reported as 7% of 2025 UK net GHG emissions.
Fuel supply is distinct from end-use combustion sectors.
The figure is part of the high-level TES sector breakdown.
It is provisional pending final inventory estimates.
No parcel fuel-supply value is inferred.

packages.title: 2025 waste 6 percent provisional share QA
facts: Waste is provisionally reported as 6% of 2025 UK net GHG emissions.
Waste-sector emissions are distinct from waste tonnage or treatment activity statistics.
Some provisional non-energy sector estimates use projections or held-constant components.
The release is territorial and national in scope.
Waste-sector national emissions are not assigned to a parcel.

packages.title: 2025 LULUCF 0.1 percent provisional share QA
facts: LULUCF is provisionally reported at about 0.1% of 2025 UK net GHG emissions.
LULUCF can contain both emissions and removals.
The provisional sector estimate is not equivalent to a site-specific land-carbon measurement.
Final inventory methods can revise the full historical series.
No parcel land-use value is inferred.

packages.title: 2025 final GHG February 2027 future-release guard QA
facts: DESNZ states final 2025 UK GHG estimates are due in February 2027.
The current 2025 publication is therefore provisional.
Formal performance reporting against emissions targets uses final rather than provisional estimates.
Future final values must not be anticipated or fabricated.
Current QA preserves provisional status explicitly.

packages.title: 2025 Q1 provisional emissions 0.3 percent increase QA
facts: DESNZ reports provisional Q1 2025 GHG emissions were 0.3% higher than Q1 2024.
Higher buildings and product-use emissions contributed to the first-quarter increase.
Quarterly changes differ from the full-year trend.
Quarterly estimates are provisional and temperature-sensitive.
A quarterly national change is not a parcel-level change.

packages.title: 2025 temperature-adjusted GHG difference QA
facts: DESNZ estimates actual 2025 emissions were about 14 MtCO2e lower than a temperature-adjusted scenario aligned to the long-term mean.
The difference is reported as about 4% of actual emissions.
Temperature adjustment is a modelled analytical counterfactual.
Buildings and product uses show the largest temperature-related deviations.
Temperature-adjusted emissions are not direct measurements.

packages.title: 2025 renewable generation 52 percent provisional context QA
facts: The provisional GHG release states renewable generation reached a record 52% share of total generation in 2025.
Generation share is an electricity-system activity measure.
Renewable generation helps explain lower electricity-supply emissions over time.
Generation share is not itself a GHG emissions amount.
No parcel emissions value is derived from the national generation mix.

packages.title: 2025 coal zero electricity-generation fuel QA
facts: DESNZ reports coal accounted for no fuel used for electricity generation in 2025 in the provisional context.
The comparison notes coal accounted for a much larger share in 1990.
Fuel mix and emissions are related but different measures.
The 2025 energy statistics used in the provisional release remain subject to revision.
No parcel electricity mix is inferred.

packages.title: 2025 nuclear and renewables 65 percent generation-fuel QA
facts: DESNZ reports nuclear and renewables together accounted for a record 65% of fuel used for electricity generation in 2025.
This is an energy-input share rather than an emissions share.
The statistic is used to explain long-term electricity-supply decarbonisation.
National generation inputs do not identify an individual consumer's electricity source.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: ONS 2024 residence-basis GHG 478 MtCO2e QA
facts: ONS estimates UK residence-basis GHG emissions at 478 MtCO2e in 2024.
Residence basis includes UK residents and UK-registered businesses wherever activity occurs.
The measure aligns with National Accounts concepts.
Residence-basis emissions differ from territorial emissions.
The national residence total is not a parcel measurement.

packages.title: ONS household 25.9 percent residence-emissions share QA
facts: ONS reports households were the largest single contributor when compared with individual industries in 2024, at 25.9% of residence-basis emissions.
Industrial emissions collectively represented the remaining larger aggregate share.
The household figure is residence-based rather than territorial.
A household-sector percentage does not identify emissions of a specific dwelling.
No cadastral assignment is made.
